title: Marcia Ann Gillespie, Editor in Chief of Essence and Ms., Has Died
summary: She became editor in chief of Essence at age 26, and later ran the feminist magazine Ms. She was 82.

title: Trump Administration Imposes Sanctions on Megaspeed, Singaporean Firm at Center of Nvidia Scandal
summary: The administration added Megaspeed to the entity list, a trade blacklist, after weeks of sparring among top officials on the decision.
caption: Megaspeed’s addition to the list will prevent companies from shipping U.S. technology to the firm without first obtaining a government license.

title: With Jensen Huang’s Return as C.E.O., Trump Effectively Overrode Nvidia’s Board
summary: Nvidia’s board said Mr. Huang would not be back. But President Trump, who pushed for Mr. Huang’s reinstatement, effectively overrode the board, governance experts said.
caption: On Monday, Nvidia said that the board had “voted unanimously” to bring Jensen Huang back as the company’s leader.
authors: Kalley Huang, Jordyn Holman, Lauren Hirsch and Ryan Mac

title: Trump’s Extraordinary Nvidia Intervention Sidelines National Security Concerns
summary: President Trump’s move to put Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia caps his indifference to the warnings of his own intelligence agencies.
caption: “I’m doing it for the country,” President Trump told CNBC on Monday shortly after Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.

title: Pressure Builds at American Airlines as It Lags Delta and United
summary: American flies more travelers than any other U.S. carrier, but debt, fuel costs and mistakes have left it losing money while other big airlines report billions in profits.
caption: American Airlines executives say they have a turnaround plan. Analysts largely say it is making the right moves but is years behind.

title: 25 Years of DealBook Moments
summary: These photographs are drawn from events since DealBook began publishing that have left an indelible mark on business, policy and culture. We’re still feeling their ripples today.
caption: First responders at Ground Zero on Sept. 11, 2001.

title: DealBook Summit 2026: Rein in A.I., but Don’t Pause It
summary: A panel of experts said protections on artificial intelligence could be adopted without stifling the technology’s development.
caption: A DealBook task force made up of leaders in technology discussed “Artificial Intelligence and the A.G.I. Horizon.” From left, Max Hodak, Dan Hendrycks, Michael Barbaro, Lila Ibrahim, Mati Staniszewski and Clément Delangue.

title: DealBook Summit 2026: Groundbreakers Tell What Is On Their Minds
summary: Leaders from a range of disciplines who led talks at the summit about global issues responded to questions in advance. Their answers have been lightly edited.
caption: Andrew Ross Sorkin spoke with more than a dozen prominent figures from the worlds of business and politics, including Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

title: How Huang’s Return Rewrote Corporate America’s Rules
summary: The reinstatement of Jensen Huang atop Nvidia, following pressure from President Trump, shattered norms for corporate governance. What comes next is unclear.
caption: Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s co-founder, is back leading the company at the center of the artificial intelligence boom.
authors: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe, Sri Muppidi and Ian Mount

title: DealBook Summit 2026: After the Upheaval From the Midterm Elections, Who Has the Edge in 2028?
summary: Are the Democrats’ gains in the midterm elections lasting? Or just another swing of the political pendulum?
caption: The “2026 Midterm Elections” task force discussed the aftermath of the midterms. From left, Stacey Abrams, Alyssa Farah Griffin, David Axelrod, Maggie Haberman, Jonathan Swan, David Urban, Morris Katz and Dan Senor.

title: DealBook Summit 2026: Help Wanted to Succeed in an A.I. World
summary: While young people are facing daunting challenges in the labor market, there are ways to improve the chance of landing a good job.
caption: “The Future of Work and Purpose” task force discussed the challenges facing young people in finding jobs and careers. From left, Chloe Malle, Ryan Gellert, Emma Grede, Jodi Kantor, Andrew Ng, Mike Rowe and Ramit Sethi.

title: DealBook Summit 2026: The Cost of Being Pragmatic in a Chaotic World
summary: At the summit marking DealBook’s 25th year, business leaders explored the dangers of mistrust in turbulent times.

title: Trump’s Nvidia Push Shows Companies’ Importance in Global Economic War
summary: Presidents before him have bailed out companies in times of national crisis. Mr. Trump went further: He staked the fortunes of the United States on those of a favored chief executive.
caption: Jensen Huang in Las Vegas in January. He was reinstalled as chief executive of Nvidia, less than two weeks after resigning.

title: Young New Yorkers Are Losing on Kalshi, City Council Says
summary: An investigation into prediction market companies found that 18- to 20-year-olds in New York City are losing money at a high rate.
caption: An ad for the prediction market platform Kalshi above the entrance to Madison Square Garden in New York City.

title: Top Aviation Officials Were Traveling When F.A.A.’s Nationwide Ground Stop Halted Flights
summary: Transportation administrators and some key executives for the contractor handling an equipment upgrade were in transit on Nov. 13, highlighting that Friday can be a bad day for something to go wrong.
caption: L3Harris Technologies signage being displayed above the company’s booth at Special Operations Forces in Tampa, Fla., in May.
authors: Kate Kelly, Nicholas Nehamas and Karoun Demirjian

title: ‘Carthage Resident Al Gore’ Buys His Hometown Tennessee Newspaper
summary: The Carthage Courier announced this week that the former vice president was buying the weekly paper, which has been publishing since 1913.
caption: Former Vice President Al Gore at the United Nations climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, this month. He was announced this week as the new owner of The Carthage Courier newspaper in Tennessee.

title: From Chinese Factory Town to the Nvidia Scandal: The Rise of Alice Huang
summary: The woman whose role has become a focus of the Nvidia spying saga grew up in a small town built around a weapons factory. Her jump to finance and the tech world paralleled China’s own.
authors: Paul Mozur, Keith Bradsher, Mara Hvistendahl, Michael Forsythe and Ana Swanson
tags: Ministry of State Security of the People's Republic of China

title: Stock Markets Slip as Nvidia and A.I. Stocks Erase Some of Monday’s Rally
summary: Shares have veered wildly for days, pushed and pulled by the drama at Nvidia and the rise and fall of Anthropic’s stock after its blockbuster public offering.
caption: Shares of Nvidia dropped a day after they surged on the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as the company’s chief executive.

title: Phone Reservations Are Back at Restaurants. Humans May Not Be Included.
summary: Against all odds, restaurants still get phone calls. A number of new services — some running on A.I. and some staffed by people — are vying for the chance to answer.
caption: The operators at Broome Street Concierge field calls, texts and emails on behalf of six restaurants.

title: Black Friday Deals Starting Earlier This Year? It’s Not Just in Your Head.
summary: Some shoppers have “Black Friday fatigue” from sales that began as early as the first week in November.
caption: Sales-seeking holiday shoppers in 1999, back when Black Friday was just one day.

title: More (and More) Black Friday Travel Deals
summary: The bargains are plentiful this year, and they include deep discounts on resorts, cruises, safaris and more.

title: Blanche Downplays Questions Over Nvidia as Investigators Examine Company’s Customers
summary: Justice Department investigators have gathered evidence of Nvidia’s high-powered computer chips being illegally diverted by other firms to China, according to people familiar with the inquiries.
caption: “I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said.

title: Putting Socially Conscious Investments in 401(k) Plans Could Get Harder
summary: The Labor Department has, once again, proposed a rule that may discourage workplace retirement plans from adding investment options based on environmental and social considerations.
caption: Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said the proposed rule “makes clear that retirement plan fiduciaries must make investment decisions solely in the financial interests of workers and retirees, not to advance political or social agendas.”
